solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Inoculant worked non-stop (9)

indicatorNotes.worked: letters that are worked are kneaded into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A vaccine that did its job around the clock.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'worked' as 'was effective', but it is the instruction to rework INOCULANT, which uses exactly the letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is continual never pauses.

entries.clue: Stop talking to leader of union supporting Conservative grandee (3,3)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
first letter of 'union'
a toff is a posh, upper-class person

annotation.surface: Snubbing a Tory bigwig who has been backed by a trade union leader.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue U 'supporting' C puts U beneath C. Toff is British slang for a well-to-do, upper-class person.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: you cut off a friend when you end contact and refuse to speak with them.

entries.clue: Nosy neighbours always saw a lot at first (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take each word at its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Neighbours, Always, Saw, A, Lot

annotation.surface: Prying neighbours who always seem to see everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nosy' wants to mean prying, which is what the surface is about; here it means 'of the nose', as nasal does.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful literal reading: nosy taken as 'to do with the nose' is what nasal means.

entries.clue: Wishful thinker that is accepting Muhammad, say (8)

indicatorNotes.accepting: one piece accepts another inside it
indicatorNotes.say: Muhammad is an example of someone called ALI

blocks.note: id est, Latin for 'that is', written i.e.
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

annotation.surface: Someone full of hopes who embraces the teachings of a great figure.
annotation.walkthrough: The religious reading of Muhammad is the misdirection; it is the boxer Muhammad Ali. 'That is' must be spelt out in full Latin, not as IE.
annotation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: an idealist chases how things ought to be, often hoping against reality.

entries.clue: Aunt regarded university bad for student (13)

indicatorNotes.bad: letters gone bad are spoilt, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
U is the standard abbreviation for university
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An aunt who thinks going to university is a poor choice for a young person.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'bad for student' the aunt's opinion; 'bad' is the anagram signal, and 'for' just points to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by a broader term: an undergraduate is one kind of student, working towards a first degree.

entries.clue: Circuits fail to maintain standard we’re told (4)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: what we are told we hear, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

blocks.note: to lapse is to slip below a standard

annotation.surface: Electrical circuits that fall short of the required standard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' suggests electronics; here it means rounds of a racetrack.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the racing sense: each time round a track is a circuit.

entries.clue: Image most choose (3)

indicatorNotes.most: most of a word is the word less its last letter

blocks.note: PICK = choose, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Picking the picture most people would choose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most' reads as 'the majority', but it trims PICK to PIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation: pic is short for picture, any image.

entries.clue: Gift despatched in advance (7)

blocks.note: pre- means before, in advance
despatched = sent

annotation.surface: A gift posted early.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'sent early', and the wordplay says the same with the pieces in the other order.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the birthday or Christmas sense of something given.

entries.clue: Produce echo within wooden box (6)

blocks.note: Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E
a crate is a wooden box

annotation.surface: Making a sound reverberate inside a wooden crate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Echo' looks like a sound bouncing round the box; it is just the letter E from the phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb: to bring something into being.

entries.clue: Tea’s temperature affected flavour (5)

indicatorNotes.affected: letters affected by something are altered

blocks.note: tea's read as TEAS
T is the abbreviation for temperature
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: How hot the tea was changed the way it tasted.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so 'Tea’s' supplies four letters, and 'affected' reads as a verb in the surface but shuffles them with T.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the flavour of food or drink is its taste on the tongue.

entries.clue: Introduce power to remove exhaust (7)

indicatorNotes.Introduce: a piece introduced to another is put into it
indicatorNotes.to: gives the destination of the introduced piece

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to delete is to remove

annotation.surface: Fitting more power to get rid of exhaust fumes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a noun about fumes; it is the verb meaning use up.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to use up resources until none are left.

entries.clue: Traditional belief family role is changing (8)

indicatorNotes.is changing: the letters of ROLE change their order

blocks.note: your folk are your family
ROLE rearranged

annotation.surface: Old-fashioned ideas about who does what at home are shifting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'family role' as one phrase about gender roles; the two words split into separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: folklore is the body of customs and beliefs handed down in a community.

entries.clue: Amphibian beginning to wriggle in trap (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of 'wriggle'
a net is a trap

annotation.surface: A newt starting to squirm once caught.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a caught creature starting to squirm; 'beginning to' takes just one letter of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the newt is one example of an amphibian, alongside frogs and toads.

entries.clue: Protest about one traitorous US politician (8)

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
c = circa, about
a rat is a traitor, one who betrays

annotation.surface: A demonstration against a politician seen as a traitor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a container instruction here but C, short for circa, as in dates.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Democrat belongs to one of the two main US parties.

entries.clue: Religious education’s pressing being born again (9)

blocks.note: RE = religious education, plus the 's
pressing = urgent

annotation.surface: Religious teaching is urgently needed for those being born again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Born again' points to evangelical religion to match the surface; the answer only means reviving. RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: something resurgent is rising again, as if reborn.

entries.clue: Unrestrained harangue involving a member of parliament (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: one piece involves another, taking it inside

blocks.note: a rant is a harangue
a as itself
MP = member of parliament

annotation.surface: A wild tirade that drags in a parliamentarian.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a politician getting an earful; the harangue is only the outer shell, split after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: growth or behaviour that is rampant runs wild, unchecked.

entries.clue: Continue to feel tired? This may be about alcohol (6)

blocks.note: to flag is to tire
to go on is to continue, as in 'on!'

annotation.surface: Keeping going while worn out — maybe drink is to blame.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'about alcohol' means physically around it, as a vessel is. The pieces come in the reverse of clue order, with 'to' as glue.
annotation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or beer, so it is literally around alcohol.

entries.clue: Can see about spiritualist’s meeting (6)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A medium announcing they can see what surrounds the sitting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can see about' reads as 'will deal with'; 'about' is the signal to rearrange CAN SEE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a seance is a gathering where a medium tries to reach the dead.

entries.clue: Insolence about male’s lameness (4)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece goes about, around, another

blocks.note: lip = cheek, insolence
M is the abbreviation for male
surface padding, the possessive glue before the definition

annotation.surface: Cheeky talk about a man's disability.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lip' for cheeky talk is a British idiom: 'Don't give me any lip.'
annotation.definitionFit: Near-synonym as nouns: a limp is the uneven walk that lameness causes.

entries.clue: Throw one’s weight behind Scottish barrister (8)

blocks.note: a verb phrase meaning support or champion
the title used in Scotland for a courtroom lawyer

annotation.surface: Backing a lawyer from north of the border.
annotation.walkthrough: In Scottish law, advocates are the equivalent of English barristers, the lawyers who argue in the higher courts.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to champion a cause, and a regional noun for a Scottish barrister.

entries.clue: Friend since penning note (5)

blocks.note: ago = since, before now
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A pal who has been writing a note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, which suits 'note', but it means enclosing, as sheep are penned.
annotation.definitionFit: Loanword: amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

entries.clue: Part of shoe pinched, losing time (4)

indicatorNotes.losing: the piece named next is taken away

blocks.note: pinched = stole
T is the abbreviation for time; removed

annotation.surface: A shoe that pinched until it wore in over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' reads as a tight shoe; it is slang for stole.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by part: the underside of a shoe, the bit that meets the ground.

entries.clue: US breakfast loaf endlessly cooked by nan (7)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.cooked: the letters are cooked into a new order

blocks.note: nan and gran are both grandmother
LOAF without its last letter, LOA, cooked into OLA

annotation.surface: Grandma bakes a loaf, American breakfast-style.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nan' is not the Indian bread, tempting beside 'loaf' and 'cooked': it is British for grandmother, GRAN, which comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: Granola, toasted oats with nuts and fruit, is a breakfast food mainly called that in the US.

entries.clue: Shower reportedly sit on the throne (5)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: a report is heard, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

blocks.note: a shower is a spell of rain

annotation.surface: Someone showering, or perhaps sitting on the loo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The throne' is British slang for the toilet, and a shower is in the bathroom, but the throne is a monarch's.
annotation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, to occupy the throne.

entries.clue: Fanatic beheaded king once (3)

indicatorNotes.beheaded: the word loses its first letter, its head

blocks.note: Cnut (Canute), king of England, Denmark and Norway, without its first letter C

annotation.surface: A zealot who executed a former monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' suggests regicide; here it is the king's name that loses its head.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in 'a fitness nut'.

entries.clue: Conductor’s chosen baton perhaps used with energy (9)

blocks.note: the elect are the chosen, as in 'president-elect'
a baton is one kind of rod
surface padding that joins the last piece on
E is the symbol for energy

annotation.surface: An orchestra conductor's chosen baton, wielded with gusto.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all orchestra, but the conductor is electrical. The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves.
